title: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 Level 1
provenance: Generated offline by tools/build_asvs_pack.py from OWASP/ASVS tag v5.0.0_release (commit 5cf9b032440be53ce345ab3c130fda46ba1ce7a2), 5.0/docs_en/OWASP_Application_Security_Verification_Standard_5.0.0_en.flat.json, SHA-256 8201b20eec2908c3380ac600c91c8ba746346fbb808859366abb232027532311: the 70 Level 1 rows of 345, with upstream identifiers and text unchanged, annotated with MoonMind's evidence classification and OWASP Top 10:2025 mappings. A later edition or level is a new pack, never an in-place edit.
license: CC-BY-SA-4.0. An adaptation of the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0, distributed with its license and notice in moonmind/security/packs/owasp-asvs, apart from MoonMind's Apache-2.0 source.
attribution: Requirement text: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0, https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/v5.0.0_release, and category names: OWASP Top 10:2025, both by the OWASP Foundation under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). MoonMind selected the Level 1 rows and added evidence classification and mappings; the adaptation is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. OWASP does not endorse MoonMind or certify conformance.
conclusions: Per-requirement OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 Level 1 conclusions from scoped evidence. A clean scan satisfies no requirement that needs review; MoonMind makes no ASVS conformance claim.
limitations: Level 1 only: 70 of the release's 345 requirements. Levels 2 and 3 can be built from the same file but are not offered until their evidence paths are reviewed.

Coverage is mostly not deterministic. Of 70 requirements: 1 partial installed-rule check plus review; 64 agent review or reproduction only; 4 organisational documentation; 1 not assessable here. No requirement declares complete objectives, so a clean scan satisfies none.

Web and API procedures are the security-review Skill's web-api-methodology catalog, referenced by ID; a retained methodology plan and results report their coverage as tested, partially tested, blocked or untested.

Known-vulnerability (with KEV and EPSS priority where feed data exists), secret, misconfiguration, dynamic-code and TLS findings are grouped by OWASP Top 10:2025 category. That lens is directional and partial, grants no coverage and never reports a category as passing.
A09:2025, A10:2025 cite ASVS V16, which has no Level 1 requirement, so this pack maps nothing to them.

requirements.title: Browser Origin Separation
requirements.summary: Verify that, if the application does not rely on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin requests to use sensitive functionality, these requests are validated to ensure they originate from the application itself. This may be done by using and validating anti-forgery tokens or requiring extra HTTP header fields that are not CORS-safelisted request-header fields. This is to defend against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF).

requirements.title: OAuth Authorization Server
requirements.summary: Verify that the authorization server mitigates refresh token replay attacks for public clients, preferably using sender-constrained refresh tokens, i.e., Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) or Certificate-Bound Access Tokens using mutual TLS (mTLS). For L1 and L2 applications, refresh token rotation may be used. If refresh token rotation is used, the authorization server must invalidate the refresh token after usage, and revoke all refresh tokens for that authorization if an already used and invalidated refresh token is provided.
requirements.applicability: Applies when the application is an OAuth authorization server with public clients.
